deep.reconstruction:
Problem (E238, §§XXVI–XXIX): find the Euler buckling load of a pin-ended column AC of height a whose flexural rigidity varies along the axis. Put s = α + βx/a; the rigidity is EI(x) = Ekk·s^{4λ}. The equilibrium equation is EI·y'' + P·y = 0. Write P = n²β²Ekk/a². Then it becomes d²y/ds² + n² s^{−4λ} y = 0.

Euler's general solution has the form y = R·sin(ζ + n/v − Φ), where v is a function of s, tan Φ = Q/R, and ζ is a constant. Buckling occurs when the phase grows by π between the two hinged ends.

On this page λ = 1/3, so EI ∝ (α + βx/a)^{4/3}. Here v = −1/(3s^{1/3}) and tan Φ = 1/(3n s^{1/3}), so the phase is ζ − 3n s^{1/3} − arctan(1/(3n s^{1/3})).
- In modern terms, z = 3n s^{1/3} is the argument of a half-integer-order Bessel function, Z_{3/2}. That is why the solution is elementary: sin z − cos z/z ∝ √(1+1/z²)·sin(z − arctan(1/z)).
- End C (s = α), y = 0: ζ = 3nα^{1/3} + arctan(1/(3nα^{1/3})).
- End A (s = α+β), phase = π: 3nα^{1/3} + arctan(1/(3nα^{1/3})) − 3n(α+β)^{1/3} − arctan(1/(3n(α+β)^{1/3})) = π. This transcendental equation fixes n (n is negative), and then P = n²β²Ekk/a².

Small-β analysis with α = 1:
- The tangent subtraction formula gives −nβ + arctan(nβ/(1+9n²)) = π.
- Linearising the arctan gives −9n³β/(1+9n²) = π, so |n| ≈ π/β is large.
- Euler's first estimate is −nβ = π + β²/(9π), i.e. P = (π + β²/(9π))²·Ekk/a².
- Carrying the approximation further he gets P = π²(1+β/3)²·Ekk/a² ≈ π²(1 + 2β/3)·Ekk/a². The rigidity runs from Ekk at C to (1 + 4β/3)Ekk at A.
- Check: the leading phase relation −3n[(1+β)^{1/3} − 1] = π gives nβ = −π/(1 − β/3 + …), hence P ≈ π²(1+β/3)². This agrees with first-order (Rayleigh) perturbation: for a hinged column with linearly varying EI, P ≈ π²·(mean EI)/a², and the mean here is 1 + 2β/3.

The next page treats finite β. With β = α = 1 it gives n = −4.0505 and P = 16.4065·Ekk/a²; I verified the approximate value −π/(3(2^{1/3} − 1)) = −4.0289.
errors: The first approximation −nβ = π + ββ/(9π) is inconsistent in order. Replacing ∛(1+β) by 1 + β/3 drops the term −nβ²/3 ≈ πβ/3, which is O(β) and far larger than the retained β²/(9π). So P = (π + β²/(9π))²Ekk/aa is wrong at first order in β. Euler himself corrects this in the next sentence to P = π²(1+β/3)²Ekk/aa.

In the A-end condition the second arctangent appears as 'A tg 2/(3n∛(α+β))' (the scan reads like '2/3:∛'). It must be arctan 1/(3n∛(α+β)), as the following line confirms. This is either a misprint in the original or a transcription error.
The writing '= π = −9n³β/(1+9nn)' silently uses arctan u ≈ u. This is legitimate only because n turns out large; Euler acknowledges this a posteriori.

ideas.what: Buckling load of a hinged column with power-law varying flexural rigidity EI ∝ (α+βx/a)^{4/3}, solved in closed form via an amplitude–phase representation
ideas.modern_name: Euler buckling of tapered (non-prismatic) columns; Bessel equation of half-integer order 3/2 with elementary solutions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E238, 1759); Bessel-function treatment of tapered columns later (e.g. Dinnik, early 20th c.)
ideas.where_published: E238, Mém. Acad. Berlin 13 (1757/1759); discussed by Truesdell, Opera omnia II.11(2)

ideas.what: Integrability of y'' + n² s^{−4λ} y = 0 in finite terms for special exponents (here 4/3)
ideas.modern_name: Riccati / Daniel Bernoulli integrable cases; half-integer Bessel functions
ideas.where_published: E238 and Euler's Riccati papers; Institutiones calculi integralis

ideas.what: Small-taper perturbation P ≈ π²(1 + 2β/3)Ekk/aa, equal to π² times the mean rigidity
ideas.modern_name: First-order (Rayleigh-quotient) perturbation of the buckling eigenvalue
ideas.where_published: E238 (this page), as a special-case asymptotic

deep.surprise_reason: These are known results of E238, already reviewed by Truesdell. The small-β asymptotics, which effectively anticipate Rayleigh-type mean-stiffness perturbation, are a minor nicety, and the order inconsistency is self-corrected by Euler. Nothing appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'A tg 2/(3n∛(α+β))' should read 'A tg 1/(3n∛(α+β))' (if the original prints 2, it is a misprint).
In the arctan subtraction formula the second term should be 'A tang 1/(3n∛(α+β))' (the scan shows '3:' for '3n').
Page signature 'Ll 3' and catchword 'XXIX.' are correctly transcribed.
